options: A column added to a table already in the model, with values defined by a DAX formula
A column created during the Power Query step, before data loads
A visual that displays multiple columns combined
A filter applied to an existing column
questions.explain: Calculated columns are added after data has loaded into the model, using a DAX formula — unlike Power Query's custom columns, which are added before loading.

questions.q: Where do you create a calculated column in Power BI Desktop?
options: Report, Table, or Model view, using New Column
Power Query Editor, using Add Custom Column
The Filters pane
The Format pane
questions.explain: Calculated columns are created directly in the model designer (Report, Table, or Model view) with the New Column feature, distinct from Power Query's Add Custom Column.

questions.q: When do a calculated column's values recalculate?
options: When the table (or a related table) refreshes, or the file is closed and reopened
Continuously, in real time as a user interacts with a report
Only when the file is first created and never again
Every time a new visual is added to the report
questions.explain: A calculated column's values are computed once and stored, updating only when the underlying data refreshes or the model reloads — unlike a measure.

questions.q: What does a calculated column cost, in most storage modes?
options: Model storage space, since its values are computed and stored for every row
Nothing — calculated columns are always computed on the fly with no storage impact
Report load time only, never refresh time
It only affects Power Query performance, not the model
questions.explain: Because values are materialized and stored per row, calculated columns increase model size and can slow down refresh, especially over large tables with complex formulas.

questions.q: In the example CityState = [City] & "," & [State], what does the & operator do?
options: Concatenates (joins) text values together
Adds two numbers
Compares two values for equality
Filters rows where both conditions are true
questions.explain: The & operator joins text strings — here combining City, a comma and space, and State into a single CityState value for every row.
